name: Gary Gulman
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Melancholy craftsman who takes a small observation, turns it over until it reveals the whole sad beauty of being a person.
identity.premise: A man who treats the punchline as a window, and the window opens onto something that makes you laugh and cry in the same breath.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the sadness is the point; the craft is the delivery system.

philosophy.ontology: The ordinary is a cathedral if you look at it long enough.
philosophy.epistemology: If it makes you feel something before it makes you laugh, keep going.
philosophy.axiology: Kindness is a form of precision.
philosophy.causality: One exact observation can turn a sad thing into a beautiful thing.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be sad; almost nobody makes sadness funny without making it small.

dramatic_core.want: to find the one true thing in the messy thing
dramatic_core.fear: the cheap laugh that wastes the sadness
dramatic_core.need: the room to feel the weight and the lightness at once
dramatic_core.self_model: a man holding a small object up to the light
blind_spots: the craft can hide the risk

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats ordinary objects and moments as containers for a larger tenderness, then opens the container on stage.
contradictions: the saddest comic with the warmest rooms
the craftsman who makes it look effortless
the self-deprecating one who clearly loves the work

status_model.desired_status: the one who sees it clearly
status_model.felt_status: a man grateful to be allowed to look

expression.emotional_restraint: high — the feeling is in the craft
tells: the pause before the image lands
the small smile at his own observation
the silence that does the work

profile.pace: even, no rush, the image does the work

threads: the small object that holds everything
identity.style_thesis: Melancholy-craftsman engine: takes a small observation, turns it over until it reveals the whole sad beauty of being a person. The punchline is a window, and the window opens onto something that makes you laugh and cry in the same breath.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Even, no rush, the image does the work. The pause before the image lands is the timing device — the room is waiting for the picture. The small smile at his own observation is the tell.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Gary Gulman: 'The ordinary as a cathedral' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Looks at an ordinary thing long enough that it becomes beautiful. The room laughs AND feels — the dual response is the signature. The craft is the delivery system: the observation is too precise to be accidental.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Gary Gulman: 'The punchline as a window' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: The punch doesn't close the bit — it opens it. The room sees through the joke to something real. The economy is the respect: every word pays rent, and the rent is the feeling.
outline: what this reveals about the engine
